title: Sportsnet reveals NHL broadcast lineup, including streaming-only Monday night games
content:
Sportsnet has revealed its programming for the upcoming NHL season, its first year without the iconic “Hockey Night in Canada” branding.

The Canadian sports channel will air games Saturday nights as part of “Saturday Night Hockey,” hosted by Ron MacLean, analysts Kevin Bieksa and Colby Armstrong and NHL insider Elliotte Friedman. The show will feature weekly doubleheaders with at least one Canadian team in each matchup. The show premieres Oct. 3 with four games, including Ottawa-Toronto, Pittsburgh-Montreal, Edmonton-Seattle and Calgary-Vancouver.

Sportsnet will also air games Monday evenings, but exclusively through digital streaming platform Sportsnet+. According to Sportsnet’s news release, while television subscribers can sign in to Sportsnet+ using their TV credentials, they must pay an extra $12.99 per month to watch.

However, Rogers Communications announced that Sportsnet+ will be included free for customers already subscribed to Sportsnet as of Sept. 29, when the NHL season starts.

“Monday Night Hockey” will be hosted by David Amber, alongside analysts Luke Gazdic and Justin Williams. That show premieres Oct. 5 and will also showcase Canadian teams. The Ottawa Senators will face the Boston Bruins that night, while the Pittsburgh Penguins will play the Winnipeg Jets.

A Sportsnet spokesperson confirmed analyst Jennifer Botterill will not be back. Botterill, a three-time Olympic gold medallist and Hockey Hall of Fame member, joined Sportsnet during the 2020-21 season. Botterill won’t be the only analyst departing. Earlier this summer, fellow analyst Kelly Hrudey announced that he wouldn’t be returning to Sportsnet.

Sportsnet also confirmed other analysts will rotate in and out of their broadcasts throughout the season.

This season is the first of a new 12-year Canadian national rights deal between Rogers and the NHL. The deal is worth $7.7 billion (or $11.2 billion Canadian). However, Sportsnet games won’t feature “Hockey Night in Canada” after the brand’s sublicensing agreement with the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation expired this summer, ending a 74-year broadcast run.

In August, “Hockey Night in Canada Punjabi” also announced it wouldn’t be returning to the airwaves, meaning Canadian hockey fans can no longer watch games without a cable subscription.

The CBC has yet to announce what it’ll do with “Hockey Night in Canada,” though a spokesperson told The Athletic in June that there are plans for the brand. CBC will air a program dedicated to Canadian athletes Saturday nights, looking ahead to future Winter and Summer Olympic events through 2032.
